sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Arakajú language' (stub): extinct Cariban language of Pará, extinct after 1820, Arakajú incorporated into the Aparai; cites Martius 1867, Kaufman 2007 (Wayana branch), Nimuendajú 1948, Gildea 2002; Croatian Wikipedia 'Arakajú jezik' repeats the Loukotka wordlist
sources.note: Nothing; no vocabulary or phonology beyond the seven Loukotka/Martius words.

sources.citation: Durbin, Marshall. 1977. A survey of the Carib language family. In Ellen B. Basso (ed.), Carib-Speaking Indians: Culture, Society and Language (Anthropological Papers of the University of Arizona 28), ch. 2. Tucson: University of Arizona Press.
sources.note: Classification and migration narrative only; notes von den Steinen added Aracaju data to Adam's comparative list; no phonology for Aracaju (no stress/accent discussion anywhere in the chapter).
sources.venue: Anthropological Papers of the University of Arizona 28

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. p. 202 and comparative table (Karaib stock, Eastern languages).
sources.note: Nothing. Entry reads: 'Aracajú or Uaraguazú - extinct language mixed with many Tupi elements, once spoken on the Gurupatüba and Parú de Leste Rivers, Pará. [Martius 1867, vol. 2, pp. 17-18.]' plus a 13-word comparative table (head u-pupu, eye seresa, water tuna, fire uapto, sun chichi, moon yasüe, arrow uárapára, man apükaua) copied from Martius.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1948. Little-known tribes of the Lower Amazon. Handbook of South American Indians vol. 3, pp. 209-211 approx. (BAE Bulletin 143). Washington: Smithsonian Institution.
sources.note: Only other work cited for the Arakajú at all; ethnographic (location on the Gurupatuba/Paru de Leste, absorption into the Aparai). Would settle identity, not stress; no phonological content expected.

sources.note: Speculative long-range etymology of animal names; p. 343: 'En Araquajú, qui est sans doute le même que l'Apalai, on rencontre beaucoup de mots tupi, néanmoins il appartient à la famille Karib.' No phonology content.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1924. Langues américaines: famille Caribe. In Antoine Meillet & Marcel Cohen (eds.), Les langues du monde (Collection linguistique 16), p. 660. Paris: Champion.
sources.note: Classification sentence only: 'Sur la rive gauche de l'Amazone, entre son embouchure et le rio Negro, on rencontre les Apalai (Aparai) sur le Jary, le Parú et le Curuá, sans doute identiques aux *Arakwayú (Araquajú) signalés sur le Parú par les anciens auteurs', with a footnote that Arakwayú contains many Tupi words; index 'Arakwayú 660.. Araquaju 660'. No phonology.

sources.citation: Goeje, C. H. de. 1906. Bijdrage tot de Ethnographie der Surinaamsche Indianen. Supplement zu Internationales Archiv für Ethnographie, Band XVII. Leiden: E. J. Brill.
sources.note: Araquaju forms (ghuriman, ghabau, ghuyary, parauté, yapoko, papiko, mamko, arimina, tracaja) appear only as parenthetical cognates in the Kaliña/Trio/Upurui animal and kinship vocabularies. The only stress remark (' = klemtoon; observations incomplete, no fixed rule) concerns de Goeje's own Surinam recordings, not Araquaju.
sources.venue: Supplement zu Internationales Archiv für Ethnographie, Band XVII

sources.citation: Adam, Lucien. 1896. Matériaux pour servir à l'établissement d'une grammaire comparée des dialectes de la famille Tupi (Bibliothèque linguistique américaine XVIII). Paris: J. Maisonneuve.
sources.note: Cites ~13 Araquaju forms (jasûe, urû, se r-esâ, apükáua..) in comparative Tupi sets. §6 'Voyelles accentuées' gives a generic Tupi-Guarani rule (accent on a final stable vowel, else on the vowel before a final consonant) drawn from Guarani/old Tupi grammars — not a statement about Araquaju and not usable for arac1235.

sources.citation: Steinen, Karl von den. 1892. Die Bakaïrí-Sprache: Wörterverzeichniss, Sätze, Sagen, Grammatik; mit Beiträgen zu einer Lautlehre der karaïbischen Grundsprache. Leipzig: K. F. Koehler's Antiquarium.
sources.note: Nothing for Araquajú: 5 scanned hits, all single forms inside cognate sets ('Roucouyenne, Apalai chichi, Araquajú xixi, Kumanagoto chich'; 'Pimenteira mäcü, Araquajú mecu, Palmella meco'; 'Zu den unteren Stämmen: Araquajú uapto xixi, Apiaká campot titi'). The only accent remark in the book ('Der Accent auf der letzten Silbe') concerns Bakairi.

sources.note: Nothing; confirms that Martius 1867 is the only descriptive reference (Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less).

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, II: Wörtersammlung Brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Leipzig: Friedrich Fleischer. pp. 17-18 ('ARAQUAJÚ. Uara-guaçú, grosse Männer.')
sources.note: Nothing. The entire attestation is a ~50-item Latin-glossed wordlist (aqua tuna, ignis uapto, sol xixy, luna yasüe, homo apükaua, arcus coelestis uaimy uárapára, deus tupána..) with sporadic acute accents but no grammatical or phonological remark. Martius's general orthographic note (pp. 29-30, preface to the Tupi dictionary) says the acute accent 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' - a transcription convention, not a statement about Araquajú.

sources.citation: Spix, Johann Baptist von & Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius. 1831. Reise in Brasilien.. in den Jahren 1817 bis 1820 gemacht, Dritter Theil. München. pp. 1324-1325 (Villa de Almeirim).
